Drone.title: Drone
Drone.description: Represents a specific unmanned aerial vehicle (drone) used for missions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Drone entity.

name.description: The common name or callsign given to the drone.

model.description: The make and model of the drone, e.g., 'SpeedyBee F405 V3'.

serialNumber.description: The unique serial number identifying the drone unit.

cameraType.description: Describes how the camera is connected and its type, e.g., 'CSI Ribbon' or 'USB Webcam'.

detectionModelUsed.description: The version or identifier of the AI detection model deployed on this drone, e.g., 'YOLOv8s' or 'custom.pt'.

Operation.title: Operation
Operation.description: Represents a planned or executed operational campaign, potentially comprising multiple drone missions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Operation entity.

name.description: A descriptive name for the operational campaign.

description.description: A detailed description of the operation's goals, scope, and context.

plannedStartDate.description: The planned start date and time of the operation.

plannedEndDate.description: The planned end date and time of the operation.

actualStartDate.description: The actual start date and time of the operation.

actualEndDate.description: The actual end date and time of the operation.

status.description: The current status of the operation (e.g., 'Planned', 'Active', 'Completed', 'Cancelled').

areaOfFocus.description: A general description of the geographic area covered by the operation, e.g., 'Northern El Oued Sector A'.

Mission.title: Mission
Mission.description: Represents a single flight or survey conducted by a drone as part of an operation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Mission entity.

droneId.description: Reference to the Drone that performed this mission. (Relationship: Drone 1:N Mission)

operationId.description: Reference to the Operation this mission belongs to. (Relationship: Operation 1:N Mission)

name.description: A unique name or identifier for the specific mission.

description.description: An optional detailed description or notes about the mission.

startTime.description: The start date and time of the mission.

endTime.description: The end date and time of the mission.

areaOfFocus.description: A more specific geographic area for this particular mission.

status.description: The current status of the mission (e.g., 'Active', 'Completed', 'Finished', 'Archived').

TelemetryRecord.title: TelemetryRecord
TelemetryRecord.description: Stores a snapshot of drone flight telemetry data at a specific point in time during a mission.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TelemetryRecord entity.

missionId.description: Reference to the Mission during which this telemetry was recorded. (Relationship: Mission 1:N TelemetryRecord)

timestamp.description: The date and time when this telemetry record was captured.

latitude.description: The GPS latitude coordinate at the time of the record.

longitude.description: The GPS longitude coordinate at the time of the record.

altitude.description: The altitude of the drone in meters above sea level.

groundSpeed.description: The drone's speed over ground, typically in meters per second.

heading.description: The drone's current heading in degrees (0-359).

batteryLevel.description: The drone's battery level as a percentage.

flightTime.description: The elapsed flight time for the current mission at the point of this record, in seconds.

DetectionEvent.title: DetectionEvent
DetectionEvent.description: Records details of an object detection event identified during a drone mission.

id.description: Unique identifier for the DetectionEvent entity.

missionId.description: Reference to the Mission during which this detection occurred. (Relationship: Mission 1:N DetectionEvent)

timestamp.description: The date and time when the object was detected.

detectionType.description: The type of object detected, e.g., 'camel', 'vehicle tracks'.

confidence.description: The confidence score of the detection, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0.

latitude.description: The GPS latitude coordinate of the drone at the moment of detection.

longitude.description: The GPS longitude coordinate of the drone at the moment of detection.

ArchiveReport.title: ArchiveReport
ArchiveReport.description: Stores generated reports, summaries, or insights, especially those produced by the AI Log Insight Tool, associated with a mission or operation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ArchiveReport entity.

missionId.description: Reference to the Mission that this report summarizes or is associated with. (Relationship: Mission 1:N ArchiveReport)

title.description: The title of the archive report.

content.description: The full textual content of the generated insight, summary, or report.

generationDate.description: The date and time when the report was generated.

generatedByAI.description: Indicates whether the report was generated automatically by an AI tool.

reportType.description: The category or type of report, e.g., 'Summary', 'Anomaly Detection', 'Operational Insight'.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of the user.

params.name: droneId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific drone.

params.description: The unique identifier for a specific telemetry record.

params.description: The unique identifier for a specific detection event.

params.description: The unique identifier for a specific archive report.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and easily debuggable, prioritizing Authorization Independence and QAP (Queries Are Not Filters) compliance. 

**Authorization Independence:** This is achieved through aggressive denormalization of authorization context. Each 'Operation' document will contain an 'ownerId' field (the UID of the user who created it) and a 'members' map (mapping UIDs to roles like 'viewer', 'editor'). Crucially, for all subcollections ('missions', 'telemetryRecords', 'detectionEvents', 'archiveReports'), these authorization fields ('operationOwnerId' and 'operationMembers') from the parent 'Operation' document are *copied down* into every document in the subcollection. This means that a security rule for a 'TelemetryRecord' document, for example, can determine access by inspecting 'resource.data.operationOwnerId' or 'resource.data.operationMembers' without needing to perform a costly and transaction-breaking `get()` operation on its parent 'Mission' or grandparent 'Operation' document. This significantly simplifies security rules and ensures atomic operations.

**QAPs (Queries Are Not Filters):** The hierarchical path structure naturally helps with QAPs. When querying a subcollection like `/operations/{operationId}/missions`, the `operationId` is already part of the path, scoping the query to a specific operation. For 'list' operations on the top-level `/operations` collection, security rules will enforce that queries must include filters based on the 'ownerId' or 'members' map (e.g., `where('ownerId', '==', request.auth.uid)` or `where('members.' + request.auth.uid, '==', 'editor')`). This ensures that users can only retrieve lists of operations they are authorized to see, rather than filtering a broader, insecure dataset. For subcollections, since 'operationMembers' is denormalized, a rule can be written to allow listing if `resource.data.operationMembers[request.auth.uid]` exists, making the list operation inherently secure based on the document's own data. 

**Structural Segregation:** All documents within a given collection (or subcollection) are assumed to have a homogeneous security posture. For example, all missions within a specific operation have the same authorization context derived from that operation. The 'status' field is used for explicit state modeling, supporting features like 'Archive' pages by filtering for `status: 'Archived'` rather than segregating by access level. 

**DBAC:** Global roles are managed via a dedicated `/roles_admin/{userId}` collection. The mere existence of a document at this path signifies an administrative role for that user, simplifying global permission checks. This avoids custom claims, relying purely on database lookups.

Overall, this structure provides a clear, maintainable, and secure foundation for the Desert Scout Dashboard application.
